findings.title: small-action button no longer right-aligned
findings.body: `.small-action` is now a flex container, so its children, including this `button`, are flex items. Floats do not apply to flex items, so `float: right` is ignored. There is also no `margin-left: auto`, `flex-grow`, or `order` on the preceding `.small-action-desc` or the button to push it to the right edge, so the button will sit immediately after the description content instead of being right-aligned. This regresses the existing small-action post layout.

findings.title: Header panel right alignment depends on modern flexbox auto margins
findings.body: `.panel` is no longer floated and is right-aligned only via `margin-left: auto` inside `.contents`, which the new `flexbox()` mixin turns into a flex container. That mixin also emits legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks, but 2009 flexbox does not use auto margins for main-axis packing. Since no `box-pack: end` or equivalent fallback is provided, browsers that use those legacy declarations will not keep the panel right-aligned. If the fallbacks are meant to be supported, the header controls will be misplaced there.

findings.title: align-items mixin omits Mozilla 2009 flexbox alignment fallback
findings.body: `flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `display: -moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box` fallbacks, but this `align-items` mixin emits `-webkit-box-align` for the 2009 box model without emitting `-moz-box-align`. As a result, Firefox versions using the `-moz-box` fallback will not get the intended `center` alignment for header `.contents` or `.small-action`, nor the `baseline` alignment for `.badge-wrapper.bullet`.

findings.title: order mixin maps modern order values directly to 2009 box-ordinal-group
findings.body: The 2009 `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties start at 1, while modern `order` starts at 0. Passing the modern value unchanged means `order(1)` would map to ordinal group 1, the same as default siblings, and `order(0)` would be invalid in the old model. The old fallback should add 1 to the value. The current calls use 2 and 3 and happen to work, but the generic mixin is incorrect and will break when reused with 0 or 1.
